Name: The Hon. Edward C. Lumley, P.C., M.P.
The Hon. Gary Lunn, P.C., M.P.
James S. Lynch, M.P.
Notes: In the first federal elections in Manitoba, held on 2 and 3 March 1871, the riding of Marquette had returned two candidates. Angus C. McKay, a Conservative, and Dr. James S. Lynch, a Liberal, received the same number of votes, 282. Both men journeyed to Ottawa, swore the oath to enter Parliament, signed the roll and took their seats in the chamber, after which they immediately withdrew. Their actions followed the procedure for dealing with controverted elections. All members "returned upon double returns (are) to withdraw until their returns are determined." Subsequently, the House of Commons Committee on Privileges and Elections decided in May 1872 to give the candidates six weeks to submit lists of voters whose names they questioned. Before the six-week period had elapsed and prior to a resolution, the Commons had prorogued. Thus, the Marquette seat was not occupied during the session.
